FSPs have been shown to be effective at reducing deforestation in the short-term, but there is a lack of evidence on the long-term impacts of these policies, especially in terms of their ability to achieve synergies between conservation, livelihoods, and climate mitigation.
FSPs can improve conservation and livelihoods in some contexts, but the evidence base is too limited to draw broad conclusions.
FSPs have been shown to have positive conservation outcomes in a few cases, with mixed livelihood outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FSPs have the potential to improve livelihoods and conserve forests, but the outcomes are not guaranteed.
there are many examples of FSPs that can achieve conservation and livelihood outcomes simultaneously.
companies and other stakeholders should consider the full set of mechanisms available to them to implement FSPs and should not rely on a single mechanism.
